notes: The page is one continuous handwritten paragraph about Picard champs pinned by M and N, with no standalone display, diagram, drawing, date or letter apparatus. Its first noun is cancelled and replaced above the line by champs.

Author claim, not a reader check: sigma is obtained from the symmetry of L tensor L and is interpreted as a section of left-indexed 2N. The author says Je sais prouver (sauf erreur) that every homomorphism M to left-indexed 2N comes from a suitable Picard champ. The explicit qualification sauf erreur is retained.

Author claim, not a reader check: an obstruction is placed in Ext cubed (X;M,N), and a quoted universel/universal argument is said to make it vanish. No such argument or proof is supplied on this page.

Author claim, not a reader check: the extension labelled (*) is close to split because sections over arbitrary objects lift, described as an ensembliste section; a stronger origin in the displayed inline degree-two hypercohomology expression is then asserted.

The lifting verb disagreement, E versus underlined F, the H alphabet, and the final argument separators prompted targeted ink inspections. Mathematical expectation did not settle these readings or cause a repair.
There is no visible manuscript page number 5. H page{5} is treated as witness pagination metadata and is not imported as mspage. The archive pencil number 63 is represented only as a comment.

The long vertical and lower horizontal reproduction boundaries are not manuscript diagrams. Scattered copying flecks were distinguished from words and formulas. The low dark point between the last M and N has enough positional relevance to be retained under unsure, while its intentional status remains open.

marked_in_H indicates an H uncertainty or unreadability marker at the locus, not merely the presence of an H deletion macro. H guillemets may be house syntax, but each visible pair of high double quotation marks is explicitly recorded.
No mathematical proof event or background-assumption check was performed. checks is therefore empty; the work is visual transcription and syntax validation only.

coverage: The whole 1685 x 2362 page was viewed once for layout, followed by the supplied upper and lower full-resolution halves once each in sequence. Every physical text line, including all agreed C/H wording, was read against both witnesses, with attention to accents, final letters, punctuation, indices, prime, arrow, tensor, quotation shape, interline additions and cancelled states. Twelve distinct documented tight crops were made and each viewed once for the unresolved loci or adjacent unresolved states; no full half was enlarged again and no OCR, external source, other page or other reader was consulted. The continuous paragraph, two upper-right strokes, three interline replacements/additions, three cancelled groups and archive foliation are all represented. No omitted prose block, display or diagram was found. H omits the upper-right strokes and archive foliation in the supplied text, expands tte, adds a comma after Picard and an unsupported cancelled group before termes, and adds i.e. near the foot. The possible small dot in the final M/N gap was absent from C and is now marked uncertain. Remaining doubts are carried in place. Both recurring H capitals were inspected independently. No LaTeX compilation was run.
